payload.claim: Acceptance criteria 1 and 2 both assert that once `main` returns, 'the SIGTERM handler is the one main found, and that handler heard nothing' / 'hears neither signal'. No test in tests/test_sigterm.py ever reads `signal.getsignal(signal.SIGTERM)` after `cli.main(...)` returns inside a `with _sigterm_safety_net(): ...` block. The only `getsignal` check in the suite fires mid-teardown (inside `_wrapped_remove_container`), before the `finally` on this line ever runs, and `_sigterm_safety_net`'s own `finally` unconditionally re-installs its own captured `previous` handler after every call, which masks whatever `main` actually left behind. Replacing this line's body with `pass` (never restoring the caller's handler) leaves `_handle` permanently installed after `main` returns, yet every test in the file keeps passing, because none of them observe the handler state at that point and the outer safety net overwrites it regardless.
